renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: F1 across allele fraction bins
  description: |-
    Each bar is the F1 score of one caller in one allele fraction bin. It answers whether a caller keeps its accuracy for the low-fraction variants that are hardest to call.
    How to read: a caller that holds its F1 down to the low bins detects subclonal variants, and one that falls off there only finds the clonal ones. A missing bar is a bin with no truth variant or no call, where the ratio divides by zero, so the recipe leaves it undefined rather than zero.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn. som.py bins true positives and false negatives by the allele fraction of the truth set and false positives by the fraction observed in the query.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: af_bin
    y: f1
    color: caller
    barmode: group
    labels:
      af_bin: Allele fraction bin
      f1: F1 score
      caller: Caller

- component: table
  title: Allele fraction strata table
  description: |-
    Each row is a caller and allele fraction bin with its recall, precision, F1 and the counts of true positives, false positives and false negatives. It answers the exact numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: read the counts beside each ratio, because a high F1 in a bin with a handful of variants means little.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md

- component: advanced_viz
  id: pr_scatter
  title: Precision against recall
  description: |-
    Each point is a callset: its recall on the horizontal axis, its precision on the vertical axis, with the point coloured by its F1 score and sized by its true positives. It answers which caller finds the most true variants without adding false ones.
    How to read: the best callsets sit in the upper right. A callset far to the left misses variants, and one low on the plot adds false calls. The curves join points of equal F1, so compare callsets by which curve they sit on.
    Lines and annotations: the curves are iso-F1 contours at 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 drawn by this chart, with F1 the harmonic mean of precision and recall. Recall is tp / (tp + fn) and precision is tp / (tp + fp), as som.py defines them. No cut-off is drawn.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  kind: pr_benchmark
  config:
    show_diagonal: false
  roles:
    label: caller
    recall: recall
    precision: precision
    f1: f1
    support: tp

- component: advanced_viz
  id: confusion
  title: True and false calls per caller
  description: |-
    Each row is a callset and each cell a count of true positives, false positives or false negatives, shaded by its share of the row. It answers what kind of error each caller makes.
    How to read: a caller with a large false positive cell is too permissive, and one with a large false negative cell is too strict. Compare the rows, since the truth set is the same for every callset.
    Lines and annotations: a true positive is a variant in both the truth and the query. A query-only variant is a false positive and a truth-only variant a false negative.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  kind: confusion_matrix
  roles:
    label: caller
    tp: tp
    fp: fp
    fn: fn

- component: advanced_viz
  id: precision_ci
  title: Precision with its interval
  description: |-
    Each point is a callset's precision with a bar for its confidence interval. It answers whether two callsets really differ in precision or only appear to.
    How to read: callsets whose intervals do not overlap differ in precision. A wide interval means few calls, so the value is uncertain.
    Lines and annotations: the bars are the 95% confidence interval for a binomial proportion, computed by the Jeffreys method (som.py default level 0.95).
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  kind: metric_ci_bars
  config:
    metric_name: Precision
  roles:
    label: caller
    value: precision
    lower: precision_lower
    upper: precision_upper

- component: advanced_viz
  id: recall_ci
  title: Recall with its interval
  description: |-
    Each point is a callset's recall with a bar for its confidence interval. It answers whether two callsets really differ in the share of truth variants they find.
    How to read: callsets whose intervals do not overlap differ in recall. A wide interval means few truth variants were tested.
    Lines and annotations: the bars are the 95% confidence interval for a binomial proportion, computed by the Jeffreys method (som.py default level 0.95).
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  kind: metric_ci_bars
  config:
    metric_name: Recall
  roles:
    label: caller
    value: recall
    lower: recall_lower
    upper: recall_upper

- component: figure
  title: F1 by caller
  description: |-
    Each bar is the F1 score of a callset for one variant type (SNVs or indels), the harmonic mean of its precision and recall. It answers which caller is most accurate for each type.
    How to read: a higher bar is a better balance of finding true variants and avoiding false ones. Open the precision and recall views to see which side limits a low bar.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: caller
    y: f1
    color: variant_type
    barmode: group
    labels:
      caller: Caller
      f1: F1 score
      variant_type: Variant type

- component: card
  title: Best F1
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest F1 score among the callsets and the box shows the spread of all of them. It answers how good the best caller is and how far the others trail.
    How to read: a best F1 far above the median means the callers differ a lot. Open the precision and recall views to see why.
  column: f1
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: F1 over the callsets, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Benchmark summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a callset and variant type with its true positives, false positives, false negatives, recall, precision, F1 and their confidence intervals. It answers the exact numbers behind every tile.
    How to read: sort by F1, then check the counts, since a high ratio on few variants is weak evidence.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md

- component: card
  title: True positives by caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of true positives over the callsets, and the bars rank the callers by how many they found. It answers which caller recovers the most truth variants.
    How to read: a caller far ahead on true positives is not necessarily best, since it may also add many false positives. Compare with the false positive card.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  column: tp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: true positives, by caller

- component: card
  title: Median F1
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median F1 score over the callsets and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how accurate a typical caller is on this truth set.
    How to read: a high median with a narrow box means the callers agree. A low median points to a hard truth set or to calls that need filtering.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  column: f1
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median F1, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Recall
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean recall over the callsets, the share of truth variants they find, with the lowest and highest beside it. It answers how complete the calls are.
    How to read: a low lowest value marks a caller that misses many truth variants. A gap between lowest and highest means the callers are not interchangeable.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  column: recall
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: mean recall, with its lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: Precision
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median precision over the callsets, the share of calls that are true, with the lowest and highest beside it. It answers how clean the calls are.
    How to read: a very low lowest value marks a caller that adds many false positives and needs filtering. No cut-off is applied, because som.py defines none.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  column: precision
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: median precision, with its lowest and highest

- component: card
  title: False positives by caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of false positives over the callsets, and the bars rank the callers by how many they added. It answers which caller is noisiest.
    How to read: false positives often differ by orders of magnitude between callers. The caller leading this ranking is the first to filter.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  column: fp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: false positives, by caller

- component: card
  title: False negatives
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of truth variants missed over the callsets, with the lowest, highest and median per callset beside it. It answers how many variants the calls fail to find.
    How to read: a narrow range means every caller misses about the same variants, which points to hard truth variants such as low allele fraction ones.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  column: fn
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: compact
  caption: false negatives, with their range over callsets

- component: card
  title: F1 summary
  description: |-
    The hero number is the best F1 score, with the lowest, median and mean beside it. It answers the range of accuracy over the callsets.
    How to read: a large gap between the lowest and the best F1 means the choice of caller matters here.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/sompy.md
  column: f1
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  - median
  - average
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: F1 over the callsets
